title: A mid-broadcast revert after step4 (initiateMigration) strands the live StableStaker terminally-migrating AND paused, with recovery limited to the 14-day claimTimedOut hatch
description: Steps 1-9 run as a single atomic broadcast under simulation, but the broadcast variant uses `--slow` (one tx at a time against the live chain) and `&&`-chains a separate preview as the only gate. Any tx that succeeds in simulation but reverts live due to state divergence between preview and broadcast (window edge, pool drift changing the migrateIn shortfall, MEV/front-run on the skim or external vault) lands mid-sequence. Because `initiateMigration` (step4) is TERMINAL on the staker (no resume path; stake/withdraw/emergencyWithdraw all blocked while active) and the staker is paused (step1), a revert after step4 leaves the live staker in a state with NO clean recovery script — only `UnpauseStakerBreakGlass`/`ResumeStableStakerMigration` (cluster evidence siblings, which exist precisely because migrations here have stalled before) and, for users, `claimTimedOut` after 14 days. This is the structural sequencing root cause SHARED by M-01 (window) and M-02 (allotment): irreversible pause/initiateMigration ordered ahead of the go/no-go checks. Its two concretely-reachable, impact-driving instances are already carried at Medium; rated Low here to avoid triple-counting one shared worst-case, but kept distinct because the front-load-reversible-ops recommendation is the generic fix that closes both Mediums structurally.
impact: No theft (invariant C). Bounded availability hazard: a stalled migration and a worst-case 14-day principal lockup if any tx reverts after the step4 terminal point. A documented break-glass mitigation (UnpauseStakerBreakGlass / ResumeStableStakerMigration siblings) already exists in the cluster, which places this umbrella observation in the QA/Low band (state/sequence handling, operational hazard) on its own merits.
attackPath: 1. A tx that succeeds in preview reverts live due to state divergence (window edge, pool-drift shortfall, MEV/front-run on skim or external vault) after step4 initiateMigration.
2. Staker is already paused (step1) and terminally migrating (step4) — no clean recovery script.
3. Recovery limited to break-glass siblings (UnpauseStakerBreakGlass / ResumeStableStakerMigration) and, for users, claimTimedOut after 14 days.
recommendation: Front-load all non-terminal, reversible operations and assert ALL go/no-go conditions (window Executable for both tokens, sufficient migrator allotment, owner authorizations) in `_preflight` BEFORE step1 pause and step4 initiateMigration, so the only thing left after the irreversible point is deterministic bookkeeping. Document the break-glass recovery runbook (UnpauseStakerBreakGlass + re-run path) as the explicit fallback for a mid-broadcast strand.
evidence: closure-manifest cluster (ResumeStableStakerMigration, UnpauseStakerBreakGlass evidence siblings); stable-staker CLAUDE.md 'migration is terminal: once engaged a token's pool can never resume healthy operation'; InPlaceMigrator claimTimedOut lines 306-323 (principal-only, after migrationTimeout). side-effects.json scenarioB shows the strand state reached when migrateIn reverts.
